taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew and Flora of North America treatments and native to Texas at state scale.
look_here_first: Compare the upper bracts and hairiness. Snow-on-the-prairie has long narrow linear-to-narrowly-oblanceolate white-margined bracts and conspicuous hairs across the plant; the showy white structures are bracts, not petals.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays is documented at Purola and Travis by multiple UT specimens. No third exact project target-zone county is locked.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification; preserve the two-county HOLD.

best_field_traits: upper bracts linear to narrowly oblanceolate with white margins
conspicuous pilose hairs on stems, leaves, and inflorescence
cyathia with 4–5 glands and white petal-like appendages
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Separate from Euphorbia marginata by the much narrower upper bracts and conspicuous hairiness; do not identify either species from the white display alone.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Narrow white-margined bracts + conspicuous plant-wide hairiness strongly favor E. bicolor; E. marginata usually has broader bracts and mostly glabrous upper leaf surfaces.
